title: Denormalization Trade-offs
description: Understand when and how to denormalize for performance without breaking data integrity

data.text: Denormalization intentionally introduces redundancy to improve read performance. It should be a conscious trade-off after normalization, not a replacement for it.

data.title: Warning
data.text: Denormalization without refresh logic causes stale data. Always plan for synchronization before adding redundant columns.

data.title: Denormalized order total
data.content: Duplicate the order total to avoid joining order_items on every read.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE orders (
  order_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id INT NOT NULL,
  total DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
  item_count INT NOT NULL
);

-- Maintain total and item_count via triggers or application logic
CREATE TRIGGER update_order_totals
AFTER INSERT ON order_items
FOR EACH ROW
BEGIN
  UPDATE orders
  SET total = total + NEW.quantity * NEW.unit_price,
      item_count = item_count + NEW.quantity
  WHERE order_id = NEW.order_id;
END;

items.question: Should I denormalize by default?
items.answer: No. Start normalized. Denormalize only when profiling shows joins are bottlenecks.

items.question: How do I keep denormalized data consistent?
items.answer: Use triggers, materialized views, or application-level refreshes on writes.

items.question: Is a star schema denormalized?
items.answer: Yes. Fact tables are wide and redundant, while dimension tables are normalized.

data.title: Summary
points: Denormalize only for proven read bottlenecks
Plan synchronization for all redundant data
Use materialized views when refresh is acceptable
data.takeaway: Denormalization is a performance lever, not a design shortcut. It trades write complexity for read speed.
